svg.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous speculation: CPU and CUDA streams
svg.desc: Two rounds of the same request on CPU, compute_stream and copy_stream. R0 through R3 are recurrent depths. Synchronous acceptance follows ID readback on CPU. Asynchronous acceptance updates token and position on compute_stream, enabling the next round while copy_stream returns prior results. CPU waits end exactly at their matching readback completion. Times are illustrative.
svg.text: A small first-round difference. A growing cross-round advantage.
Round 0 / 1 = speculative iterations R0…R3 = recurrent loop depths (example d=2, D=4)
Each next round waits for CPU acceptance and commit.
GPU state joins rounds; result copy and CPU commit overlap the next round.
T · same instant in both panels
Unused here: synchronous ID readback runs on compute_stream inside collect().
Verify → read IDs → CPU Accept / update → CPU Commit → next Submit → next Draft
Start = CPU begins submit. End = CPU finishes Commit (async: includes ticket retirement). These markers cover the round’s host-visible lifetime.
compute_done = GPU work finished; copy_done = result D2H finished. Neither alone means Round End. Async round lifetimes overlap; GPU rounds stay ordered.
Round 0 / 1 = speculative iterations; R0…R3 = recurrent depths. Commit records outputs / progress and checks EOS / length; buffer reuse follows retirement.
Illustrative, not measured: slightly shorter GPU acceptance; equal Draft / Verify widths. Greedy · warm · multi_stream=True · bootstrap / cold capture omitted.
